title: Between Tides and Twilight
excerpt: From sunset over Victoria Harbour to lantern-lit autumn nights, a few moments of wandering through Hong Kong.
paragraphs: As summer gave way to autumn, I returned to Hong Kong from Shenzhen just in time for sunset over Victoria Harbour. I wandered along the Avenue of Stars as red sails drifted slowly past in the distance. The evening sky glowed orange-red, and flecks of gold danced on the water. Across Hong Kong Island, scattered lights spread from the Central piers up into the Mid-Levels. As dusk deepened, a bright moon rose quietly.

A few autumn nights unfolded in starts and pauses: the bustle of corner bars on Peel Street in Sheung Wan and the slightly tipsy evening breeze; the brilliant star lanterns in Victoria Park at Mid-Autumn; the old-world elegance that has lived on for a century at The Peninsula. Happy Valley was as lively as ever, horses racing beneath the lights as cheers rose and fell.
closing: When the wind rises, may you fly like a swallow into the tall trees; when the tide recedes, may I return like a boat to a distant shore.

coverCaption: The last light over Victoria Harbour, before the city settles into night.
